options: Ben will join the Community Cleanup.
Soye is helping Ben to put up a poster.
Anyone can join the Community Cleanup.
People pick up trash as a volunteer activity.
The poster is about the Community Cleanup.
questions.question:
[지문]
B: Good morning, Soye! What are you doing?
G: Hi, Ben. I'm trying to put up a poster, but it's not easy.
B: Can I help you? I can hold it for you.
G: Sure! Thank you for lending a hand.
B: You're welcome. What is this poster for?
G: It's for the Community Cleanup.
B: What is the Community Cleanup?
G: It's a volunteer activity. People sweep the streets and pick up trash to make our neighborhood clean.
B: That's a good idea! Can I join?
G: Of course! It is open to everyone.

다음 대화의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
questions.explanation: 대화에서 Ben이 Soye를 도와주고 있으며, Soye가 Ben에게 도움을 청하고 있다. 따라서 'Soye is helping Ben to put up a poster'는 틀렸다. 올바른 내용은 'Ben is helping Soye to put up a poster'이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever (A) [use / used] a digital kiosk before? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble (B) [used / using] kiosks.

To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying.

After the class, people said, "Now we feel (C) [comfortabler / more comfortable] with kiosks. Thank you so much!" We felt very proud.

(A)~(C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 바르게 짝지어진 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) Have you ever used - 현재완료 형태로 'used'가 맞다. (B) have trouble using - 'trouble' 뒤에는 동명사 'using'이 온다. (C) feel more comfortable - 형용사의 비교급은 'more comfortable'이 맞다.

questions.question:
[지문]
After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community. ①We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. ②We all agreed that the roads needed more lights. ③Many students complained that the roads were too narrow for cars to pass. ④With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. ⑤Now all our neighbors feel safer than before!

다음 글에서 전체 흐름과 관계 없는 문장은?
questions.explanation: 글의 흐름은 '어두운 도로' 문제를 파악하고 → 더 많은 조명이 필요하다고 합의 → 센서가 있는 조명 설치 → 이웃들이 더 안전함을 느낌으로 진행된다. '도로가 자동차가 지나가기에 너무 좁다'는 내용은 문제 해결과 관계가 없어서 전체 흐름을 방해한다.

options: Marking the plates to help students know how much food to take
Punishing students who leave leftover food at lunchtime
Collecting money to buy more food for the community
Turning off the lights in the cafeteria to save energy
Asking the principal to change the school lunch menu
questions.question:
[지문]
One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take too much food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?" The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve this problem. We thought that adding lines to food trays would be helpful. Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food. Our school principal liked ⓐ this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. It was a success! The new trays reduced a large amount of food waste!

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ this idea가 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 'this idea'는 바로 앞 문장에서 언급된 'adding lines to food trays would be helpful'을 가리킨다. 즉, 음식 쟁반에 줄을 그어서 학생들이 적절한 양의 음식을 가져갈 수 있도록 하는 것이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community. We found out (A) [that / what] some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads (B) [needed / needing] more lights. With the help of a teacher, we (C) [put / putting] up lights with sensors around the neighborhood.

다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 'found out that' - 명사절을 이끌 때 'that'을 사용한다. (B) 'agreed that the roads needed' - 과거 시제로 'needed'가 맞다. (C) 'we put up lights' - 과거 시제 동사 'put'이 맞다.

options: A scientific report analyzing global warming data
A fictional novel about a magical school
A speech introducing a club's achievements
A formal letter of complaint to the school principal
A proposal requesting funding for club projects
questions.question:
[지문]
Hello, everyone! I'm Yuna, and I'm the leader of Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club has solved some problems in our school and our community over the past few years. I want to share our stories.

다음 글의 종류로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 글의 시작이 'Hello, everyone!'이고, 자신이 클럽의 리더임을 소개하며, 클럽이 해결한 문제들과 성과를 공유하려고 한다는 내용으로 보아 클럽의 성과를 소개하는 연설(speech)이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
B: Hello, Ms. Lee. Can I help you? Your hands are empty. W: Oh, hi, Jihun. Yes, please. Can you open the door for me? B: No problem. I can also carry the books for you. W: Thank you! Please put them over there. B: Okay. Is there anything else? ①W: That's it. ②Thank you so much for helping me. ③B: You're welcome. ④Have a nice day, Ms. ⑤Lee!

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 ~ 중 문맥상 어색한 것은?
questions.explanation: B가 'Your hands are empty'라고 했는데, 이후 대화에서 W가 'I can also carry the books for you'(책을 운반해 주겠다)라고 제안하고 W가 'Please put them over there'(그곳에 놓아달라)라고 말한다. 따라서 W의 손에 책이 있어야 하므로 'Your hands are empty'는 문맥상 맞지 않는다.

questions.question:
[지문]
As you can see, your actions can make positive changes. Even the smallest acts can make _________!

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 'Even the smallest acts can make'라는 표현으로 보아, 긍정적인 변화를 일으킬 수 있다는 의미이다. 따라서 'a big difference'(큰 차이를 만들다)가 가장 적절하다.

questions.question:
주어진 대화 다음에 이어질 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

[기본 대화]
Hey, Junsu. What are you doing?

(A) Can I help you? I'll hold the bike.
(B) Hi, Amy. There is a problem with my bike. I'm trying to fix it.
(C) Sure, thank you.
questions.explanation: 자연스러운 대화 흐름: Amy가 '뭐하니?'라고 물어본다 → Junsu가 '자전거가 문제가 있어서 고쳐보고 있어'라고 대답한다(B) → Amy가 '도와줄까? 자전거를 잡아줄게'라고 제안한다(A) → Junsu가 '좋아, 고마워'라고 응한다(C)

options: Being the leader of the club
Helping people at the community center
questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before? You may think ⓐ it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks. To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ it이 가리키는 내용으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: 문맥상 'You may think it's easy'의 'it'은 바로 앞 문장의 'Have you ever used a digital kiosk before?'에서 언급된 'digital kiosk를 사용하는 것'을 가리킨다.

questions.question:
다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 바꿔 쓸 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?

- Mina lived in Europe 2 years ago.
- She still lives there.

→ Mina __________ in Europe for 2 years.
questions.explanation: 두 문장의 의미는 'Mina가 2년 전에 유럽에 살기 시작해서 지금도 살고 있다'는 것이다. 이는 과거에 시작해서 현재까지 지속되는 상황이므로 현재완료 'has lived'가 적절하다.

options: (A) too much (B) to solve (C) amount of
(A) too many (B) to solve (C) number of
(A) too much (B) to solve (C) number of
questions.question:
[지문]
One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take (A) [too much / too many] food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?"

The members of Warm Hearts gathered (B) [solving / to solve] this problem. We thought that adding lines to food trays would be helpful. Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food.

Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. It was a success! The new trays reduced a large (C) [amount of / number of] food waste!

다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
questions.explanation: (A) 'food'는 비가산명사이므로 'too much'가 맞다. (B) 'gathered to solve'는 '~하기 위해 모였다'는 의미로 부정사 'to solve'가 맞다. (C) 'food waste'(음식 낭비, 비가산)는 'amount of'와 함께 사용한다.

questions.question:
다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

B: Hi, Julie. You look worried. Can I help you?
G: Yes, I'm looking for my phone. I think I ____________.
B: Your phone will ring when I call. I'm calling you now.
G: Ah, here it is! Thank you for helping me.
B: You're welcome.
questions.explanation: 줄리가 휴대폰을 잃어버렸다고 말해야 상황이 맞다. 친구가 전화를 걸어서 울리면 찾을 수 있다는 대화의 맥락에서 'lost it'이 적절하다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중 어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 옳게 고친 것은?

Hello, everyone! I'm Yuna, and I'm the leader of Warm Hearts, a club at our school. Our club has solved ① any problems in our school and our community over the past few years. I want ② sharing our stories.

One day, our school principal ③ announce, "Our students often ④ taking too much food and waste ⑤ it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?"
questions.explanation: 'want' 다음에는 to부정사가 와야 하므로 'sharing'은 'to share'로 수정되어야 한다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)와 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞춰 영작했을 때, 6번째 올 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

(A) 당신은 이전에 디지털 키오스크를 사용해본 적이 있나요? You may think it's easy. But some people have trouble using kiosks.

<조건>
- 아래 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 문장을 완성할 것
- before / kiosk / you / have / digital / used / ever / a
questions.explanation: "Have you ever used a digital kiosk before?"의 순서로 배열되어야 하며, 6번째 단어는 'kiosk'이다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)와 같은 의미가 되도록 문장을 전환할 때, 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

As you can see, your actions can make positive changes. (A) Even the smallest acts can make a big difference!

→ A big difference ______ ______ ______ by even the smallest acts!
questions.explanation: 능동태 'can make'를 수동태로 전환하면 'can be made'가 된다. 주어가 'A big difference'이고, 행위자가 'the smallest acts'이므로 수동태 구조가 필요하다.

options: I want to play soccer with my friends.
My hobby is to collect stamps.
I went to the library to study for the exam.
It is easy to solve this math problem.
She has no time to sleep.
questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ와 문법적 쓰임이 같은 것은?

ⓐ To help them, we volunteered as digital guides at the community center. We explained every step of ordering: starting an order, choosing from the menu, and paying.
questions.explanation: ⓐ의 'To help them'은 목적을 나타내는 to부정사이다. "시험 공부를 위해 도서관에 갔다"라는 뜻의 '③ I went to the library to study for the exam'이 동일하게 목적을 나타내는 to부정사 구문이다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 (A), (B), (C) 안에서 문맥에 맞는 낱말로 가장 적절한 것은?

G: Jack, those boxes look (A) [heavy / light]. Can I help you?
B: Yes, please. Can you (B) [take / leave] this one?
G: No problem.
B: Thank you for (C) [carrying / dropping] it.
G: You're welcome.
questions.explanation: 상자들이 무거워 보여서(heavy) 도움을 청했고(Can I help you?), 상자를 가져가달라(take)고 요청한 후 들어주셔서(carrying) 감사한다는 문맥이 맞다.

options: The difficulty of putting up posters alone
Introduction to and participation in a local volunteer event
The necessity of recycling trash for the environment
How to organize a school poster contest
The danger of sweeping streets without safety gear
questions.question:
다음 대화의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

B: Good morning, Soye! What are you doing?
G: Hi, Ben. I'm trying to put up a poster, but it's not easy.
B: Can I help you? I can hold it for you.
G: Sure! Thank you for lending a hand.
B: You're welcome. What is this poster for?
G: It's for the Community Cleanup.
B: What is the Community Cleanup?
G: It's a volunteer activity. People sweep the streets and pick up trash to make our neighborhood clean.
B: That's a good idea! Can I join?
G: Of course! It is open to everyone.
questions.explanation: 대화는 포스터 부착으로 시작되지만, 핵심은 지역 자원봉사 활동인 Community Cleanup을 소개하고 참여를 권유하는 내용이다.

questions.question:
다음 글에서 문제 해결 전에 이웃 주민들이 느꼈을 심경으로 가장 적절한 것은?

We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads needed more lights. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel safer than before!
questions.explanation: 도로가 밤에 매우 어두웠다는 것은 위험한 상황이었고, 이웃 주민들은 불안하고 두려웠을 것이다. 조명 설치 후 더 안전해졌으므로 대조된다.

questions.question:
글의 흐름으로 보아, 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

주어진 문장: The members of Warm Hearts gathered to solve this problem.

One day, our school principal announced, "Our students often take too much food and waste it at lunchtime. How can we reduce food waste?" ( ① )
We thought that adding lines to food trays would be helpful. ( ② )
Students could look at the lines and take the right amount of food. ( ③ )
Our school principal liked this idea, so he changed the food trays in the cafeteria. ( ④ )
It was a success! ( ⑤ )
The new trays reduced a large amount of food waste!
questions.explanation: 교장선생님이 문제를 제시한 직후, Warm Hearts 클럽 멤버들이 문제 해결을 위해 모였다는 문장이 와야 논리적 흐름이 맞다.

questions.question:
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 우리말 (A)와 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞춰 영작했을 때, 5번째 올 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

B: Hello, Ms. Lee. Can I help you? Your hands are full.
W: Oh, hi, Jihun. Yes, please. Can you open the door for me?
B: No problem. I can also carry the books for you.
W: Thank you! Please put them over there.
B: Okay. Is there anything else?
W: That's it. (A) 저를 도와주셔서 정말 감사합니다.
B: You're welcome. Have a nice day, Ms. Lee!

<조건>
- 아래 주어진 단어를 모두 한 번씩만 사용하여 문장을 완성할 것
- me / helping / much / you / so / for / thank
questions.explanation: "Thank you so much for helping me"의 순서로 배열되어야 하며, 5번째 단어는 'so'이다.

options: 강아지들을 돌본 자신의 경험에 대해 말한다.
questions.question:
다음 대화가 끝난 직후, 'Jinho'가 할 행동으로 가장 적절한 것은?

W: Welcome to the Happy Animal Shelter. Can I help you?
B: Yes. I'm here to volunteer.
W: Can I have your name, please?
B: I'm Jinho. I love dogs, so I want to take care of them.
W: That's great! I'll introduce our puppies first.
B: They're so cute. What should I do to help?
W: While we clean the cage, take these puppies for a walk, please.
B: Okay. I'm excited to spend some time with them!
W: I'm glad. Thank you for volunteering!
questions.explanation: 직원이 "we clean the cage"하는 동안 "take these puppies for a walk, please"라고 명확히 지시했으므로, Jinho는 강아지들을 산책시키러 갈 것이다.

questions.question:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

After we solved this problem at our school, we started to look for problems in our community. We found out that some roads around our school were very dark at night. We all agreed that the roads needed more lights. With the help of a teacher, we put up lights with sensors around the neighborhood. Now all our neighbors feel safer than before!

Recognizing the potential danger of the ___(A)___ streets at night, the club members installed sensor lights to ensure the ___(B)___ of their neighbors.
questions.explanation: 원문에서 "roads were very dark at night(밤에 도로가 매우 어두웠다)"고 했으므로 (A)는 'dark'이고, "neighbors feel safer"로 표현된 주요 목적이 이웃의 안전을 보장하는 것이므로 (B)는 'safety'이다.

questions.question:
[지문]
Have you ever used a digital kiosk before?
You may think it's easy. But some people have
trouble using kiosks.
To help them, we volunteered as digital guides
at the community center. We explained every step
of ordering: starting an order, choosing from
the menu, and paid.
After the class, people said, "Now we feel more
comfortable with kiosks. Thank you so much!"
We felt very proud.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?
questions.explanation: 병렬 구조상 전치사 of의 목적어로 동명사 starting, choosing이 나열되고 있으므로 paid 또한 동명사 형태인 paying으로 고쳐야 한다. 현재완료시제에 쓰인 과거분사 used는 적절하다. 「have trouble + 동사원형-ing」은 '~하는 데 어려움을 겪다'라는 의미의 표현이므로 using은 적절하다. 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 온 동명사 choosing은 적절하다. feel은 감각동사로 뒤에 형용사 보어가 와야 하므로 comfortable은 적절하다.
